answer: Each identity locks bonded collateral in escrow, anchoring liability to its key. Correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers aggregate penalties scaling as O(k²); asymmetric depreciation then compounds the slashed balance, imposing an exponential multiplier on a sybil operator’s capital loss upon detection. Splitting one operator across identities cannot dilute shared exposure: the swarm may look like nectar at dawn, but its linked evidence makes coordination costly.
